These soils will be used for construction of three water impounding embankments. Also, they will be the source of sediment when vegetative ground cover is removed.
6. EXISTING DRAINAGE FEATURES
Drawing PBK-1014-1 shows existing site topography and major drainage areas with the major project features noted. The landscape is dissected by streams and the slopes are moderate to steep. Only small floodplains exist in the area since high stream gradients inhibit floodplain formation.
Total runoff and peak discharge from a 10-year, 24-hour storm have been calculated using methods devised by the United States Department of Agriculture, Soil Conservation Service. (1) Table I on drawing PBK-1014-1 summarizes the results of these calculations. Erosion losses from the site under existing cover conditions have been calculated for a 10-year, 24-hour storm. (2) Concentrations of total suspended solids may reach or exceed 8400 Mg/L based on total soil loss and total runoff from this storm.
7. CONSTRUCTION PERIOD
The following construction activities are considered in this plan:
a) Stream diversion
b) Reservoir borrow area operation
c) Construction yard and switchyard
d) Embankment construction
e) Relocation of County Road 171
f) Transformer yard construction
g) Temporary and permanent access roads
h) Discharge portal area
i) Transmission lines
Total runoff and peak runoff from the site during construction have been calculated for a 10-year, 24-hour storm using USDA-SCS methods. (1) The results of these calculations are given in Table II on drawing PBK-1014-2. Erosion losses from the disturbed site have been calculated for a 10-year, 24-hour storm. (2) Concentrations of total suspended solids may reach or exceed 44,000 Mg/L based on total soil loss and total runoff volume from this storm.
a) Stream diversion - The stream diversion pipe and intake structure located in the Bad Creek streambed will be placed before construction of the Bad Creek sediment basin begins. Runoff from diversion placement will drain into lower Bad Creek and Howard Creek.
